scope.method: manual source audit of research/data/bot code; data-quality numbers for daily bars re-confirmed from research/atomics/data_audit.json (not re-derived)
scope.note: research-only: no files modified, no fixes applied

summary.conclusion: The dominant defect is survivorship bias: every universe-based backtest uses today's listed/index constituents applied through up to 20 years of history. A second systematic issue is that the multiple-testing/FDR and placebo infrastructure exists (research/atomics/multiple_testing.py, core.py) but is NOT wired into any sweep; per-trade (unclustered) t-stats and best-of-N reporting remain the default. One concrete off-by-one bug (time-series value) and one broken placebo helper were found. Most findings are already self-disclosed in BACKTEST_CAVEATS.md / SELF_AUDIT.md / the trading-backtest-validation skill; the ones below are the exact code locations.

findings.issue: Universe is built from Wikipedia S&P 500/400/600 constituents AS OF TODAY (current index membership), then filtered on the last 3 months of yfinance data. Delisted / index-removed / bankrupt names are absent, so the universe back-applied through ~20y of history contains only survivors.
findings.impact: Every backtest that reads research/universe_1500.json (stmom_backtest.py, indicator_sweep.py, and any sweep importing it) is an UPWARD-BIASED upper bound. Worst for buy-the-dip mean-reversion (RSI2/STOCH/Bollinger) where the names that fell to zero are exactly the losses now missing. INVALIDATES the magnitude of all universe-based PF / avg-bp / t-stat claims; the true edge is lower.

findings.issue: load_equities() builds the cross-sectional universe from ibkr/equities/daily/*.parquet = today's listed snapshot (comment at line 176 admits it). The long-short cross-sectional momentum uses the current-listing set, so the short leg (recent losers) is missing delisted names.
findings.impact: Long-short spread is OVERSTATED (short leg biased).
findings.note: This file DOES disclose it (line 528 note field); the defect is real but self-flagged. Files that do NOT disclose it while using the same universe: indicator_sweep.py, stmom_backtest.py.

findings.issue: Corwin-Schultz (corwin_schultz_by_year) and Abdi-Ranaldo (abdi_ranaldo_by_year) spreads are computed as ONE aggregate per symbol-YEAR, using that year's ENTIRE high/low/close series (including days AFTER day t), then mapped back to every day t of the year via .map(cs_year). The per-trade cost on day t therefore uses future same-year price data.
findings.impact: The cs/ar cost-model net numbers (overnight_24h_edge.py COST['cs']/COST['ar']) are within-year look-ahead contaminated.
findings.note: Does NOT invalidate the primary conclusion: overnight_24h_edge.py:18-30 explicitly labels cs/ar 'noise-inflated UPPER BOUND' and the decision relies on tick1 (100/close, uses only current close) and flat bp costs, which are look-ahead-free.

findings.issue: Time-series VALUE backtest misaligns signal and forward return. sig[t] = spot<5y_mean (signal at month-end t); fwd = cdf.pct_change().shift(-1) so fwd[t] = close[t+1]/close[t]-1 (correct forward month); but pos = sig.shift(1) so r[t] = sig[t-1] * return[t+1]. The comment ('position set at month-end t, return realized over next month') requires r = sig * fwd (no shift). The extra .shift(1) lags the signal one month AND pairs it with a return window that starts one month later. Inconsistent under any convention.
findings.impact: The family_value TIME-SERIES result and its cost-stress table (lines 667-676) are computed with a one-month-misaligned signal. The cross-sectional value result (xsectional_futures) is unaffected.

findings.issue: shuffle_symbols() claims to 'permute predictions within each timestamp cross-section (swap across symbols)' but its body is identical to shuffle_timestamps() — a single rng.permutation(pred) over the whole array, which shuffles across time AND symbols together. A cross-sectional null must permute WITHIN each timestamp only.
findings.impact: Any downstream cross-sectional placebo using shuffle_symbols would produce an invalid null (destroys time structure too). Currently only referenced by research/atomics/test_platform.py (not wired into any backtest), so it does not invalidate an existing result today, but the API is silently broken.

findings.issue: 8 strategies reported with individual PF/t and no Benjamini-Hochberg or any correction; the FDR machinery in research/atomics/multiple_testing.py is never called by any sweep (grep: only referenced from test_infra.py). Same best-of-N pattern in edge_sweep2.py (4 families x multiple configs) and overnight_24h_edge.py (survivors_pf13_oos picks the max-cost-wall variant, with section-5 'IS-SELECTED COMBOS' itself labeled overfit).
findings.impact: Best-of-N is reported as if a single discovery; false-positive rate inflated across the batch.
findings.note: overnight_24h_edge.py does disclose section 5 as 'overfit risk -- reported for completeness', which is partial mitigation; indicator_sweep.py and edge_sweep2.py do not apply correction.

findings.issue: t = mean/(std/sqrt(n)) over PER-TRADE returns across hundreds of correlated same-day trades; each trade is treated as independent. Effective n << nominal n.
findings.impact: Reported t-stats (e.g. 't=7-9' style) are inflated upper bounds. Date-clustered t required (see stmom_backtest.py:38-44 for the correct pattern).

findings.issue: START = '2010-01-01' hardcoded. yfinance futures go back to ~2000, so the backtest (and its OOS) excludes the 2000-02 dotcom crash and the 2008 GFC.
findings.impact: OOS regime coverage is misleading; a sleeve can show a healthy OOS PF that would not survive a 2000/2008 drawdown. Reported numbers flattered.

findings.issue: COST_SCENARIOS: base = spread 3 + slippage 2 = 5bp round-trip; conservative = 10bp RT; stress = 20bp RT. Measured reality (repo's own sampler): the open-sell leg alone is ~12bp, and sub-$50 round trips are ~14bp+; the skill's own guidance is 'headline >=10bp/SIDE, stress 15-20bp/SIDE'. So even 'stress' (20bp RT = 10bp/side) sits at the low end of the real cost.
findings.impact: Cost stress understates real execution cost; strategies can survive 'stress' in this engine while failing on measured cost.

findings.issue: MAE/MFE use l.iloc[entry_i:i+1].min()/h.iloc[entry_i:i+1].max(), including the ENTRY bar's full high/low. For a close-entry trade the entry bar's intraday path happened BEFORE the position existed.
Dict key 'sharpe' is assigned np.mean([t['r'] ...]) = mean R-multiple, not a Sharpe ratio.
findings.impact: Misleading metric label in the config comparison printout.

findings.issue: dd = ((cum - peak)/100_000).min() divides by constant initial equity, not running peak; and equity curve is not recorded (only final equity).
findings.impact: Percentage drawdown understated vs peak-relative; coarse metric.

findings.issue: Trailing stop: best = max(best, h) uses today's HIGH to ratchet the stop BEFORE checking whether today's LOW triggered it (l <= stop). Assumes low followed high within the bar.
findings.impact: Standard within-bar ambiguity; slightly favorable to the trailing-stop variant.

findings.issue: walk_forward_splits() accepts purge_bars but ignores it in 'expanding' mode (only used in 'rolling' mode's train_start); embargo_bars is applied. Default purge=0 anyway.
findings.impact: Latent label-overlap risk if a caller sets purge_bars with expanding mode.

findings.issue: Signal window is hist.index[-25]..[-6] = 19 trading days (docstring says 'prior-month return skip most recent 5 days' ~21d). rebal uses .to_timestamp('M') = calendar month-end; when the last calendar day is a trading day, get_indexer(...,'ffill') + entry_i=m_pos+1 makes the signal EXCLUDE the true last trading day. Minor off-by-one.
findings.impact: Approximate, not exact, monthly momentum window.

findings.issue: Dead loop 'for s in slip_series: pass' leftover before the time-series value block.
times = set.intersection over every symbol's index; a symbol with a missing bar at t is silently excluded from that timestamp's cross-section.
findings.impact: Selection bias toward symbols that trade every 5-min slot; negligible for 40 liquid names.

findings.issue: top_decile_ret ranks predictions over the WHOLE test set (across all timestamps), not per-timestamp; top decile can be dominated by a single time regime.
findings.impact: Cross-sectional ranking metric mixed with time; weaker methodological signal.

findings.issue: Daily 'unreliable open field' (open==close) is 6.27% weighted / 3.20% median, concentrated in dead listings — NOT the previously-claimed 64-85%. 5-min data is clean (0 dup, 0 OHLC violations) except 30 flat placeholder bars (O=H=L=C, barCount=0) on 2026-02-25 10:55-11:15 for 6 symbols (feed/halt gap). 'Batched timestamps' not observed in the collectors reviewed (daily_collect.py / backfill_bars.py use session-date keys + full-timestamp intraday records).
findings.impact: Open field usable for liquid names; flat placeholder bars are a known feed-halt artifact, not real zero-volume trading.

not_audited: Full breadth of bot/live_*.py execution lanes and hardening/* were out of scope for the research-defect focus; crypto backtests not exhaustively line-reviewed.
